Guides

Picky eating

Suspicion of new food is a normal toddler stage. Growth, not the day’s plate, tells you when to ask for help.

Findings

Neophobia peaks after the first birthday. A child who ate broadly as a baby and narrows as a toddler is following a common path, not failing one.
Keep the structure and drop the negotiations. One family meal, a familiar food on the plate, no substitute dinner.
Ask for help when growth, not manners, is the worry. Falling off a growth curve, fear that looks like pain, or a diet of only a handful of foods for months is a clinical question.

What is ordinary

Food neophobia rises in the second year and then slowly falls. It probably had a survival value once children could wander toward plants. It feels personal and is mostly developmental. Children also have days of eating almost nothing and days of eating a great deal, often tracking growth spurts rather than your menu.

A few reliable foods, sometimes called accepted foods, are an asset. Build the plate around one of them plus the family food. Do not retire a food forever because it was refused twice.

What helps

Keep meals predictable. Let the child see the food without being asked to perform. Eat the same food yourself. Offer rejected foods in a different cut or next to a dip they like, still without commentary. Fifteen quiet exposures beat one dramatic tasting session.

Milk after the first birthday should not become the meal. If a toddler drinks milk all afternoon they will arrive at supper full. Water between meals, milk with a meal or a snack, in a moderate daily amount.

When it is more than picky

Talk to the health visitor or paediatrician if weight or length is faltering, if eating hurts, if the child coughs or vomits with specific textures, or if the accepted list has shrunk to a few brand-specific foods and is still shrinking. Those patterns are not solved by more pressure.

A child who is growing, playing, and driving you mad at dinner is usually in the ordinary group. The work is to stay boring and available.
